Who is going to fall into the Wint Trap this week? I'm going to avoid him and the other big faves (Gautier, Pinas) and go for King Green to get past Esteban Ribovics.
Silva earns her shot at gold at UFC 332 thanks to an 8-0 unbeaten run in UFC. Her total unbeaten run goes back 14 fights. Her last loss was to Marina Rodriguez in 2017. In January, Silva got a decision over Rosa Namajunas . Before that she decisioned Alexa Grasso and Jessica Andrade . Of her eight UFC wins, only two are stoppages. That’s a 2023 TKO over Victoria Leonardo and a spinning back kikc on Tereza Bleda the year before.
Wang doesn’t have the record Silva has, but she’s made herself notable due to the personality she brings to her fights and the build-up around them. She burst onto the scene with a brutal KO over Leonardo in 2024 (see that here ). In her next fight she was finished by Gabriella Fernandes , while a -950 favorite. Since then she’s won four decisions, including a fight with Eduarda Moura that she missed weight for and didn’t go entirely her own way. Her last fight was in July, when she took a very dull decision over Tracy Cortez .
It’s easy to see why Silva is the favorite here. She’s been very steady over her UFC career; doing what she needs to win, but also not doing anything that exciting. Wang is a little more emotional and that has led to higher highs and lower lows.
I think Silva is the more rounded and more technical fighter. Though, I also think Wang is more capable of producing a moment that can stop a fight. And I think the stage being set here, plays to the advantage of a showman like Wang.
Both these ladies prefer to keep it standing and both land at a decent clip while also being defensively sound.
Against Namajunas, Silva landed 51 significant strikes and held her opponent to just 26 (at a 27 percent accuracy). Namajunas’ career sig. strikes per minute is 3.5, so she should be landing 53 sig. strikes in fifteen minutes. And her career accuracy is 41 percent. Before this Silva held Grasso to 45 sig. strikes at 32 percent accuracy. Based on Grasso’s averages she should be landing 63. And she has a career 41 percent accuracy. So Silva, it seems, is good at making fighters throw and land less than expected.
Wang really showed up against Cortez, landing 137 sig. strikes with 63 percent accuracy. That’s the third time she’s landed over one hundred sig. strikes in a fight. The only fight that went the distance, where she didn’t break 100, was her win over Eduarda Moura. She landed just 39 there, but that’s because a lot of that fight happened on the ground.
So my big question is, can Silva drastically dent Wang’s output and, even if she does, will Wang still be landing more than Silva typically absorbs in a fight. And also, if Wang can land 130-140 sig. strikes in three rounds, how many can she land in five?
This line of thinking has me leaning towards Wang, who I also think hits harder than Silva.
I think we are due for a five round decision here, since neither of these women have a lot of stopping power. And I think Wang is going to be landing the harder looking shots throughout. Silva might chip away with leg kicks and body kicks, but I think Wang’s big swings up top will make more of a difference and that those will be the ones the judges remember.
Who wins the UFC 332 main event?
Figueiredo was submitted by Song Yadong in May (see it here ). Before that he lost a decision to Umar Nurmagomedov and won a decision over Montel Jackson . The former Flyweight champion is now 4-4 since moving up weight classes.
Talbott took a convincing decision over Henry Cejudo in December. That match seemed to suffer from the fact these two were quite familiar and possibly fond of each other. Before that Talbott took a decision over Felipe Lima . Talbott is now 11-1 as a pro, with that one loss being his famous defeat to Raoni Barcelos last year. Talbott was the -1150 favorite in that fight. Barcelos has since proved that the oddsmakers got that one wrong.
We’ve known for a while now that Figueiredo just doesn’t have the youth or size to be a factor at the upper climbs of Bantamweight. He’s been competitive against great fighters, which I think deserves a lot of credit. But he’s just not been capable of really hurting many and then pushing through to get a win. He did manage to Yan a few times in their fight, but Yan seemed to accept that in order to do what he wanted to do.
Given where Figueiredo is at in his career (and life), I’m finding it hard to pick him in this bout. Yes, Raoni Barcelos has shown us what a 40-year-old is capable of in the division and against this opponent. But Figueiredo and Barcelos are totally different fighters.
I can’t see a world where Figueiredo is able to physically impose himself on Talbott and either get him down or back him up with his striking. Talbott will look like a giant in this fight and that’s going to be significant in the clinch and in wrestling.
Historically, Talbott hasn’t been much of a wrestler, but he used wrestling to beat Cejudo. Now, he might have only done that because he was facing Cejudo and wanted to say he could take down an Olympic champion. If he’s willing to play for takedowns in this fight, I think he’ll find a lot of success with them.
I’m confident that Talbott wins, but I don’t think he stops Figueiredo. Figueiredo has great grappling and is very good at protecting himself off his back. Figueiredo also has a hell of a chin (just watch that Yan fight). His only KO losses are a knee injury and an eye injury.
All that has me looking at the over.

articles.content_orig:
The winner of Game 3 will face the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLDS.
The Phillies (1-1) face the Atlanta Braves (1-1) in Game 3 of their NL wild-card series Thursday (8 p.m., NBC).
The winner moves on to the NL divisional series to face the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Phillies have no excuse to finish their comeback.
Aaron Nola will take the mound for the Phillies , with Zack Wheeler expected to follow. The Braves will turn to reliever Ray Kerr.
"A pick-me-up game for me": Bryce Harper reflects on his roller coaster performance in Game 2 .
Here's what our columnists thought of the Phillies' gutsy Game 2 victory: David Murphy | Marcus Hayes
A couple of hours before game time, Phillies manager Don Mattingly and Braves counterpart Walt Weiss both used the same phrase when addressing questions about the availability of certain pitchers in Thursday night’s decisive game three.
“I’d say all hands on deck today,” Mattingly said when asked if Zack Wheeler will be available in the bullpen on three days rest.
It’s a somewhat ironic choice of words for Mattingly, given the number of Phillies relievers he seems determined to avoid using.
ATLANTA — Jhoan Duran's availability to pitch in the Phillies' win-or-go-home Game 3 of the wild-card series will be determined in the same way that it was for Game 2.
Duran will play catch and report back on how he feels.
"I'm expecting him to be good," interim manager Don Mattingly said here Thursday in a pregame meeting with reporters.
ATLANTA — Remember when Brandon Marsh started in right field for the National League in the All-Star Game?
Three months later, he isn't in the Phillies' lineup for an elimination game.
Amid a deep second-half slump, Marsh fell into a platoon in which he typically starts only against right-handed pitchers. But he will begin Game 3 of the wild-card series on the bench here Thursday night, even though Braves lefty Ray Kerr is an opener and expected to pitch only a few innings.
The Phillies are trotting out a very similar lineup to Game 2, especially at the top. The first five spots remain unchanged. Bryan De La Cruz replaces Brandon Marsh in the sixth spot with lefty Ray Kerr starting. The only other change from the last game is J.T. Realmuto and Justin Crawford swapping spots at the bottom of the order.
That also means that Edmundo Sosa, who came up limping after trying to beat out a ground ball in the ninth inning of Wednesday's win and had to leave the game, is back in the lineup for the Phillies. He'll bat seventh.
Meanwhile, the Braves have changes up and down the lineup against righty Aaron Nola after facing lefties in Games 1 and 2.
All hands on deck pic.twitter.com/5xsFKBNLyn
The Phillies have Aaron Nola and Zack Wheeler lined up Thursday to face the Braves in Game 3 , a game that seemed unlikely to be played when Bryce Harper lost that fly ball in the afternoon sun. But we know what happened next. Atta’ boy, Harper.
Now the Phils have every advantage to become just the fourth team in the new postseason format to win a wild-card series after dropping Game 1.
The key to winning this series was forcing a third game as Atlanta entered the playoffs unsure who would be its third starter. They’ll use Ray Kerr, a reliever who returned in August from Tommy John surgery, as an opener likely followed by Grant Holmes as a bulk reliever.
The Phillies’ Game 2 win over the Braves was a lot of different things.
It was playoff baseball at its finest, not to mention its most hazardous to a fan’s cardiac health. It was a showcase: of the razor-thin margins that will determine which of these two teams advances, and of the strengths that once again have the Phillies on the verge of an NLDS berth.
Mostly, though, Game 2 was a story. First, of failure. Then, of overcoming it.
ATLANTA — Alec Bohm sat behind a microphone for what could have been the last time as a Phillie on Wednesday morning, and he reflected on his 6½ seasons in the majors as a Phillie, supporting rosters dotted with future Hall of Famers. He will be a free agent this winter, and his inconsistent play combined with his occasional truculence have led to assumptions that he will be moving on .
Then, five hours later, Bohm, hitting in the No. 4 spot, rocked the winning home run in the 10th inning of Game 2 of the wild-card series against the Braves. The Phillies took a 4-3 lead, which held up in the bottom of the inning as rookie Andrew Painter dealt the third of his three scoreless innings, and the season was saved.
With it, Bohm might have saved his future in Philadelphia and erased some of the less jubilant moments of his past.
ATLANTA — Facing their third elimination game in five days, the Phillies will hand the ball to their longest-tenured player.
Aaron Nola will start Thursday night in Game 3 of the best-of-three wild-card series, according to a major league source. The Phillies had not yet announced a starter.
Nola will be on full rest four days after starting on only two days’ rest and lasting only one inning in a desperate gambit to clinch a playoff spot last Saturday night. But the Phillies will take an “all hands on deck” approach to their pitching plan, interim manager Don Mattingly said Wednesday.
The Atlanta Braves are turning to lefty Ray Kerr as their Game 3 starter.
Kerr, a reliever who returned in August from Tommy John surgery, as an opener likely followed by Grant Holmes as a bulk reliever.
And we thought Don Mattingly’s options were limited this postseason.
Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly was picked apart after Game 1, so how about the Braves not using Robert Suarez in Game 2?
Suarez returned from the injured list in September and pitched twice in the season’s final week before being added to the postseason roster. He was lights out as Atlanta’s setup man before injuring his elbow in June and his velocity last week was about where it was preinjury.
So how does Suarez — who the Braves signed before the season to a three-year contract worth $45 million — not get used in Game 2?
The winner of Game 3 between the Phillies and Atlanta Braves will punch a ticket to the National League divisional series to face the No. 2 seed Los Angeles Dodgers.
The Phillies went 2-4 against the defending World Series champs this season, though the last time the two teams faced off was way back in July. It would also be a replay of last year's NLDS, which the Dodgers handily won 3-1.

articles.title_orig: Putin Says World Is Living Through a Dangerous Moment, Warns West Not to Escalate
articles.title_zh: Putin Says World Is Living Through a Dangerous Moment, Warns West Not to Escalate
articles.content_orig:
President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday the world was living through a dangerous moment and warned the West not to escalate a standoff over Ukraine by threatening the Russia n exclave of Kaliningrad, which Moscow has made clear it would defend with nuclear weapons if necessary.
Locked in a war in Ukraine which he said Russia had no choice but to launch in order to safeguard its own security, Putin said Russia had no plans to attack any European country and wanted to coexist peacefully.
But he reiterated that Moscow would resort to all weapons in its arsenal, including nuclear ones, if its most westerly territory — Kaliningrad, which is wedged between Poland and Lithuania — was threatened.
"If it comes to a direct attack on the Russia n Federation – in this case, we are referring to Kaliningrad, and perhaps other territories as well — the question of the Russia n Federation deploying all the weapons at our country’s disposal will, of course, inevitably and immediately be on the agenda ," Putin told the Valdai Forum of international Russia experts in Moscow.
"This is inevitable," he said.
Putin said Russia realized it would be facing "an enemy [NATO] twice our size."
"And we will have to make use of our competitive advantages in this struggle. Yes, of course, France and Britain are nuclear powers — we understand that perfectly well and are fully aware of it," he said. "But no one else possesses the kind of weapons that Russia has today. That is our competitive advantage."
Putin's comments followed a diplomatic note which NATO said this week it had received from Russia , warning the Western military alliance it would be ready to resort to nuclear weapons if NATO attempted to cut off Russia 's Baltic exclave.
Russia 's warning highlighted Moscow's urgent concern at what it has presented as a growing NATO threat to Kaliningrad, a heavily militarized Russia n territory that is slightly bigger than the U.S. state of Connecticut. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said the alliance had responded by emphasising that it was a defensive alliance and that nuclear threats were not helpful.
Relations, already dire since Putin's decision to send troops into Ukraine in 2022, have worsened this year, with European governments accusing Moscow of stepping up a "hybrid war" on the continent through acts including sabotage and arson.
Russia denies that, and rejects repeated statements by Western politicians that it is gearing up for a possible military attack on a NATO country.
Putin warned that cycles of escalation in international conflict could quickly lead to dangerous scenarios.
"We must realize that the moment when nothing can be changed any longer may come very quickly and unexpectedly for everyone. The logic of escalating, increasingly harsh retaliatory measures leads to a fatal point of no return," he said.
"At the heart of this escalation lie arrogance and overconfidence. This is a path to the brink of the abyss. All the more so today, when the arsenals of the world’s leading powers contain weapons capable of destroying all life or, at the very least, reducing the Earth to a catastrophic state," Putin said.
"Can we be certain that these weapons will never be used? Well, of course not. We must bear this in mind and avoid such an outcome," he added.
Putin, who said he was ready for a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump if a proper agenda was worked out first, ruled out the idea of stopping Russia n strikes on Ukrainian targets in the Black Sea area, while conceding that Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries across Russia had cost Russia 1% of its gross domestic product (GDP).
He said Russia was now responding to Ukraine in kind.
But while he cast Western help to Kyiv when it came to launching deep strikes inside Russia as a future threat, he said Moscow was not planning to attack arms factories in Europe which supplied Ukraine "tomorrow."

articles.title_orig: Supreme Court to decide lawfulness of Trump’s immigrant detention policy
articles.title_zh: Supreme Court to decide lawfulness of Trump’s immigrant detention policy
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court said Thursday it will consider whether immigrants subject to deportation can be held in detention indefinitely while their cases are adjudicated.
The eventual ruling could endorse or end a key feature of President Donald Trump’s hard-line immigration crackdown.
The case was among three the court took up ahead of the justices’ return to action Monday for a new nine-month term following a summer break. Rulings in all three are due by the end of June.
The focus in the first case is whether such immigrants should have a chance to argue at a bond hearing that they can be released while the deportation process moves forward, which was standard practice under previous presidents.
The justices will hear a Trump administration appeal in the case of Ricardo Aparecido Barbosa da Cunha, a man from Brazil who originally entered the United States in the mid-2000s.
He was detained following a traffic stop in Norwood, Massachusetts, in September 2025. He sued, and a federal district judge ordered that he be released. The New York-based 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals upheld that decision on appeal.
Lower courts have been divided on the issue, although the majority have sided with immigrants who have argued that the federal law the Trump administration cites to hold them without a bond hearing only applies to people detained near the border.
Since last summer, the Trump administration has sought to apply that federal law to anyone deemed to have entered the United States illegally, even if they are nowhere near the border and have lived in the country for years.
Several cases on the issue are pending at the Supreme Court.
“Try as it might, the government cannot twist the law to detain immigrants for months or even years on end without a bond hearing. Not only is it cruel and inhumane; it is unlawful,” Michael Tan, a lawyer with the American Civil Liberties Union representing various detainees, said in a statement.
In court papers, Solicitor General D. John Sauer, representing the Trump administration, called the issue a “critically important question of immigration law.” The policy removes a “perverse incentive” whereby people who evade detention when they enter the United States get treated more leniently than those detained at the border, he added.
The litigation, Sauer said, is “disrupting the orderly administration of immigration law.”
Thousands of people have already been detained under the policy, which could apply to millions of immigrants if expanded, and many of them have contested it. The case does not concern immigrants who have been convicted of certain crimes. Under federal law, they can be detained until they are deported, although separate lawsuits have raised questions about whether they should be eligible for bond hearings, too.
ACLU lawyers said in court papers that the Trump administration policy is a “radical reinterpretation” of immigration law, pointing out that some of those being detained were young children when they crossed the border.
Those challenging their confinement are not a flight risk or a potential danger to the public, ACLU lawyers say.
Lawrence Hurley is a senior Supreme Court reporter for NBC News.

articles.title_orig: Microsoft makes Windows settings backup the default in 26H2
articles.title_zh: Microsoft makes Windows settings backup the default in 26H2
articles.content_orig:
Annual update installed. You're up to date, so nothing seems to have changed. Wait a minute...
Windows 11 26H2 is out, and Microsoft has enabled Windows settings backup by default, a move that could send administrators scrambling to opt out where they once had to opt in.
The latest release hasn't made a lot of shockwaves in the community featurewise. Users with up-to-date versions of 25H2 will unlikely notice much difference – 26H2 has the same code base, delivered via an enablement package. It even has the same set of known issues, although all are now "mitigated" in one way or another.
However, administrators will spot several important changes. The end-of-support clock is reset, and Microsoft has flipped some switches behind the scenes; notably, enabling Windows backup and restore (formerly Windows Backup for Organizations) by default.
The service, which was previously off by default, backs up a device's settings and a list of installed Microsoft Store apps. The idea is that when a user moves to a new device, a restore can happen during setup. Microsoft also listed an objective of the service as allowing "organizations to transition to a cloud-first approach for managing devices and user settings."
The problem is that many organizations are prohibited from sending this data to the cloud. As a result, the default-on setting won't apply in privacy-sensitive regions such as those covered by the EU Digital Markets Act, or in sovereign and restricted environments.
For many others running Windows 11 26H2, it'll now be enabled by default on eligible devices – Entra joined or Entra Hybrid joined. Unless an administrator has explicitly said no to the functionality, the act of installing the update will flip the switch, and the backups will begin.
Administrators will rightly be wary of anything that switches from opt-in to opt-out, even something so apparently useful and innocuous as a backup. Why wouldn't you want your users to be able to leap to a new device with ease? That assumes their data is also in the cloud, of course, since this only backs up settings and a list of Windows apps. Backing up data is something else entirely.
That is the real issue with the change. The release of Windows 11 26H2 isn't particularly exciting in itself, but flipping a long-standing opt-in to opt-out as part of it is likely to set more than a few nerves jangling. ®

articles.title_orig: Winner of Nikon microscopy photo contest faces criticism over AI usage
articles.title_zh: Winner of Nikon microscopy photo contest faces criticism over AI usage
articles.content_orig:
The organizers of a highly regarded scientific photography contest are reviewing this year’s winning entry following criticism over the use of AI.
Nikon has announced that it’s “carefully re-reviewing the information” provided by Ning Xu, whose short video of intricate cell movement won the annual Small World In Motion competition in September.
At the time, Xu was a researcher at Tsinghua University in China. He’s since joined National University of Singapore as a research fellow, according to Nikon .
In a post on LinkedIn on Saturday, Nikon said that, “Xu is respectfully complying and has provided detailed technical documentation outlining the microscopy equipment, imaging methods, and processing techniques used to create the source video.”
Astonishing footage of abnormal cell movement in lungs wins 2026 Nikon video microscopy prize
The video captures the abnormal beating of airway cilia — hairlike structures that protrude from cells within the human body — in a child living with primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD), a rare genetic disorder, Nikon said at the time the winner was revealed.
In mid-September, Nikon announced that the video, which was created using an advanced microscopic imaging tool, had won the 16th annual Nikon Small World in Motion competition.
Last week, the competition posted the video on LinkedIn, where it received a number of critical comments from other users.
Edward Phelps, an associate professor at the University of Florida, said there were “many serious problems with this video.” He said that some of the biological structures shown in the footage do not behave as expected. “The microscopy community deserves an explanation from Nikon,” Phelps added.
Ian Donovan, a PhD student at UT Southwestern Medical Center, wrote that the video has “an embedded SynthID watermark identifying synthetic/AI-generated content.”
Xu replied to some of the criticism on Nikon’s LinkedIn post, saying that “AI was not used to generate the experimental movie, the cilia, or their motion.”
“It was applied afterwards to the reconstructed grayscale data to distinguish and color structures with similar morphology,” he added.
“A more detailed description of the optical system and quantitative analysis of the ciliary motion are currently being prepared for publication, and we hope to make these available soon,” he said.
“For me, the important distinction is between using an image to make a scientific claim and using visualization to communicate the beauty of scientific data,” added Xu. “Both can have a place, as long as we are clear about which is which.”
CNN has contacted competition organizers for comment.
CNN has tried contacting Xu for comment directly and via the Tsinghua University and the National University of Singapore.

articles.title_orig: Whale sinks yacht in South Pacific, sailors rescued alive 18 hours later
articles.title_zh: Whale sinks yacht in South Pacific, sailors rescued alive 18 hours later
articles.content_orig:
A sperm whale cracked the hull of a yacht sailing in the remote South Pacific, forcing four sailors into a day-and-night fight for survival on the high seas.
Crew members on the 52-foot Tai Tam told AFP on Thursday of their weekend encounter with a pod of sperm whales 250 nautical miles north of tiny Norfolk Island.
"There was sort of a loud thud. The whole boat was pushed sideways," said Australian Jemma Cooper, who was thrown from the steering wheel by the force of the blow.
Not knowing at first what had happened, she noticed a brown discoloration in the water and a sperm whale.
"We looked out to our port side, and there were six to eight, a pod, of whales there. So then it became clear that that's what it was," she told AFP.
Her husband Jeremy Cooper said he was sleeping below deck when the impact woke him.
"It was pretty immediately evident it was very serious," he said.
"All the steering gear was smashed on the starboard side, and there was a significant amount of water coming in," Jeremy told AFP.
At 1 p.m. New Zealand time on Saturday — about 30 minutes after the whale collision — they activated an emergency beacon.
"We declared a full mayday," said New Zealand crew member Terry Hetherington, adding they spent the next few hours bailing out as much water as they could.
The Royal New Zealand Air Force flew a P-8A Poseidon patrol plane to the area to establish radio communications and coordinate the rescue, the military said in a news release , which included images of the rescue.
French crew member Martin Jaffre said the whale collision left several gashes in the hull and cracked the fiberglass structure, as well as breaking the steering.
"We could no longer steer the boat, and a boat with no steering quickly becomes a problem," he told AFP.
Jaffre battled to slow the incoming water with anything to hand, including expansion foam, and swam below the boat to inspect the hull, his crewmates said.
The sailors tried to stay aboard as long as possible, struggling to stop the engine getting clogged and bailing by hand.
Late at night, they abandoned the boat and transferred to a life raft in calm seas and under a full moon.
In the early hours of Sunday morning, they cut the tether to the yacht, fearing it might drag them down. Soon after, it slipped beneath the waves.
The New Zealand military released dramatic drone video of the yacht plunging below the water's surface and the crew ultimately being rescued.
A 470-foot container ship, the MV Sofrana Surville, rescued the sailors at 6 a.m. on Sunday, the New Zealand military said — about 18 hours after their encounter with the sperm whale.
Even the rescue was scary as the giant ship approached their tiny life raft, recalled Jeremy Cooper.
But within half an hour they had scaled a ladder to join their rescuers, have a cup of coffee and chat with the captain, he said, ruing the end of their Pacific holiday voyage.
"It was wonderful, wonderful, and just a terrible, terrible ending — but luckily no loss of life."
Rescue Coordination Centre Operations Manager Mike Clulow praised the efforts of the rescue team and the yacht's crew.
"This was a well-coordinated and executed rescue," Clulow said. "The crew of the yacht did all the right things, and it was unfortunate to have struck a whale in open water. They were well prepared and the early activation of their EPIRB (Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacon) was key to helping get them to safety. It is an excellent reminder that being prepared when going to sea can save your life."
Adult male sperm whales measure between 50 and 60 feet. They are considered a "vulnerable" species by the nonprofit International Union for Conservation of Nature. Sperm whales reproduce once every five to seven years and have experienced significant population decline. The species is under threat from noise pollution, plastic consumption and ship strikes.
The incident in New Zealand marks at least the second time in less than two months that a whale has sunk a boat. In July, a whale that surfaced for air slammed into a New Jersey fire department's boat, sinking the ship with firefighters on board.  Someone on a personal watercraft nearby and a boater helped rescue the firefighters from the water.

articles.title_orig: A ‘loophole’ in New York’s rape law may have shut the door on criminal charges in the Cornell case. It’s not the first time
articles.title_zh: A ‘loophole’ in New York’s rape law may have shut the door on criminal charges in the Cornell case. It’s not the first time
articles.content_orig:
Resurfaced allegations of a gang rape at a Cornell University fraternity house have renewed outrage over what experts call a legal “loophole” in New York’s – and other states’ – sexual assault laws that can make it nearly impossible for survivors to seek justice if they voluntarily consumed alcohol or drugs before an assault.
At issue in the Cornell case is the fact that the woman, identified only as Jane Doe, says she drank alcohol and accepted drugs the night in 2024 she alleges she was sexually assaulted for hours and advertised as “free p*ssy” by someone in a Chi Phi fraternity member group chat.
The Tompkins County district attorney this week offered many words to describe Doe’s account of how the men assaulted her: disgusting, repugnant, offensive, morally reprehensible.
But he did not call it a crime.
“The young men who engaged in that conduct were morally wrong. It was disgusting, and so she reported that to the police, and the police investigated it. That does not mean – if it’s morally wrong or disgusting or offensive, all those things – it does not mean that the penal law was violated,” prosecutor Matthew Van Houten said on CNN’s “The Situation Room.”
His response has left many asking the same question: How could that be?
The answer, sexual assault survivors and their advocates say, is what’s come to be known as the voluntary intoxication “loophole” or “exclusion,” a gap in the law that exists in about 19 states in the US. It’s one reason countless assaults have gone unprosecuted, experts say, and adds to the overwhelming number of barriers survivors face in seeking justice.
Under one section of New York law , a person is guilty of rape if they engage in sexual contact with someone who is “incapable of consent by reason of being mentally disabled or mentally incapacitated.”
Here’s the “ loophole :” A person is only considered “mentally incapacitated” under the state law if they were temporarily unable to understand or control their actions due to the influence of a narcotic or intoxicating substance administered to them without their consent – or to any other act done to them without their consent.
Jane Doe willingly drank alcohol before arriving at the fraternity house, where members led her upstairs, she stated in a recent state lawsuit. Then, after the men surrounded her and pressured her to take ketamine – a dissociative anesthetic the Drug Enforcement Administration notes has been used to facilitate sexual assault – some of them sexually assaulted her for hours, according to the lawsuit, which seeks damages against seven men allegedly involved.

Doe told police she was OK with an initial encounter but said she did not consent to sexual contact later in the night, according to a six-page statement obtained by CNN detailing comments Doe made to investigators in the weeks after the alleged assault. She also described being physically hit.
In addressing Doe’s lawsuit allegations, Van Houten this week referenced her voluntary drug use in explaining the decision not to bring criminal charges, which he said were considered when she first came forward shortly after the incident.
“The facts provided by Jane Doe’s statement do not allege that she was either rendered incapable of controlling her own conduct or that any drug was administered to her without her consent,” he said.
In New York and elsewhere, every legislative session presents a chance to amend the laws around sexual assault. The Cornell rape case has laid bare a systemic failure within the criminal justice system, said Stefan Turkheimer, vice president for public policy at RAINN, an anti-sexual violence organization.
Legislation to remove New York’s voluntary intoxication exclusion has been introduced annually for at least the past eight years without success. Some lawmakers have been pushing for change for even longer.
New York’s law was originally written in the 1990s to address cases where people were “roofied,” or drugged without their knowledge, rendering them unable to consent, New York Assemblyman Jeffrey Dinowitz told CNN.
“Under the current law, somebody being voluntarily intoxicated, which happens all the time, is a virtual get-out-of-jail-free card for somebody who commits a sexual assault,” said Dinowitz, a Democrat. “And that’s just not right.”
In 2019, Dinowitz tried to change that with legislation preventing the use of a victim’s voluntary intoxication as a defense in sex crimes where the victim was incapacitated. He sponsored it again in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026. Despite the consistent support of victims’ advocates and other lawmakers, the legislation has never made it to the House for a vote.

“To me, it’s kind of like there’s a binary choice here,” Dinowitz said. “Either you’re on the side of the survivors of sexual assault or you’re on the side of the people who commit the sexual assaults. And I know where I stand.”
Opponents have raised concerns that it’s difficult to nail down the exact point at which a person becomes too drunk to consent. Others have questioned whether a new law paving the way for more prosecutions would disproportionately impact people of color due to existing biases in the criminal justice system.
The crime of sexual assault can make survivors feel incredibly alone, RAINN’s Turkheimer pointed out. “The way to heal is to come forward, share with others, and find solace and protection and justice in that sharing – but that depends entirely on whether or not it is safe for that person to come forward,” he said.
In the Cornell case, Jane Doe experienced “a textbook reaction to trauma” that likely meant the loss of criminal evidence, her attorney, Thomas Giuffra, told CNN on Thursday. Her “internal processing went from denial, to shame and ultimately acceptance that she had been raped by people that she thought were her friends.”
One of Jane Doe’s roommates couldn’t “really remember her ever kind of citing that she had said yes to anything that occurred,” the roommate said of the first hours after Doe returned home the morning of October 20, 2024, according to documents from a university review of the accusations obtained by The New York Times .
Still, it wasn’t until Doe read an online forum about Greek life shortly after the encounter that “I had ever heard the narrative change that I wasn’t a whore and that I was assaulted,” she told investigators, according to Title IX files compiled as part of the school’s formal process for investigating allegations of sexual harassment and assault.

Doe “took steps to protect herself and sought STD testing and UTI treatment at Cornell Health on October 22,” her lawyer said, noting Doe told a health care worker she contracted the UTI in a ‘traumatic way.’” But she was not offered expert consultation or a rape kit, which would “likely have revealed DNA which would have been significant information for a criminal investigation,” Giuffra said.
By November 3, 2024, Jane Doe apparently concluded she’d been assaulted at the October party, sending a text to one of the men she would allege was involved: “let’s be clear that 90% of what happened that night was not consensual. i was given more key than i can remember,” she wrote, using a shorthand for ketamine, “and i know that i told u i felt uncomfortable and i didn’t know anyone in the room.”
But by “the time she went for the rape kit on 11/7 all of the DNA evidence was gone,” Giuffra told CNN.
“We really need to think about who we’re protecting and why,” Turkheimer said. “If we are actually trying to encourage survivors to come forward, we have to have people and systems who prioritize their safety.”
Changing these laws state by state has proven difficult – but not impossible.
